about.title: Pacific Grove Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Pacific Grove is a small coastal city, but its households, garages, and small businesses use the same appliances, tools, vehicles, and consumer goods found anywhere else in Monterey County — and defects don't discriminate by zip code. Whether it's a kitchen appliance that malfunctioned in a home near Sunset Drive, a faulty bicycle part on the Rec Trail along Ocean View Boulevard, or defective equipment used at a local business, California law gives injured people a real path forward. Because product liability claims here often rest on strict liability, you generally don't need to prove the manufacturer was careless — only that the product was defective and that the defect caused your injury. That said, these cases move quickly and depend heavily on preserving the product itself. Our team evaluates what happened and explains your options under California law directly.

whyChoose.title: Why Pacific Grove Residents Choose Us

items.title: Strict Liability Can Simplify Your Case
items.desc: California generally allows injured people to hold manufacturers, distributors, and retailers responsible for a defective product without proving negligence. That can make the path to accountability more direct than in other injury cases.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Under California law, liability can extend beyond just the manufacturer to distributors and retailers in the supply chain, giving you more than one avenue to pursue.

items.title: Guidance on Preserving Evidence
items.desc: We advise you early on keeping the product, packaging, and receipts intact — details that matter a great deal in defect claims and are easy to lose if you wait.

items.question: Do I need to prove the manufacturer was careless?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California product liability claims often proceed under strict liability, meaning you generally need to show the product was defective and that the defect caused your injury, rather than proving negligence. We can review your situation and explain which theory fits your case.

items.question: What should I do with the product that injured me?
items.answer: Keep it exactly as it was at the time of the injury, along with any packaging, manuals, or receipts. In Pacific Grove, where many injuries involve everyday household or outdoor equipment used near places like Forest Avenue or the coastal trails, the physical product itself is often the most important piece of evidence in the claim.

items.question: Is there a cost to speak with an attorney?
items.answer: No. We offer a free initial consultation, and we typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation. There's no obligation to move forward after that initial conversation.
